title: Auto-rotate should be disable-able and enable-able via system tray
line: The Display Configuration applet in the system tray now has a switch to turn automatic screen rotation on and off.
explanation: Automatic rotation could only be changed in System Settings > Display Configuration > Orientation, which is a lot of steps for something people often want to turn off or on just for a moment (tablet on a stand, reading in bed). No applet offered a quick toggle. The Display Configuration applet (the one in the system tray's hidden items, with Screen Layout and Presentation Mode) now shows a "Rotate Screen Automatically" switch whenever a connected screen supports automatic rotation. It reflects whether rotation is in effect right now and sets the screen's auto-rotate policy through libkscreen: off sets Never, on sets Always, or "only in tablet mode" (the default) when the device is currently in tablet mode.

commits.message:
plasmoid: add a switch to rotate the screen automatically

Turning automatic rotation on or off meant going to System Settings each
time, even though it is often only wanted for a moment. The applet now
shows a switch for it when a screen supports automatic rotation.

BUG: 503732

media.caption: Display Configuration applet on master with a rotation-capable screen: no way to turn automatic rotation on or off.
With the fix: a "Rotate Screen Automatically" switch, here turned on (KWin's policy becomes "always").
